qs.situation: A customer's order is promised '5 working days' from today. Next Wednesday is a public holiday and your office is shut.
options: Only Saturdays and Sundays are days off; the holiday still counts as a working day
Public holidays are also skipped, using the national holiday list
Public holidays are skipped, using our own company holiday list

qs.situation: An order comes in on a Saturday and the promise is '1 working day'. When does the clock start?
options: It starts from the next working day, Monday, so the answer is Tuesday
Saturday counts as a day on the clock, so the answer is Monday
It is treated as if the order came in on Friday, so the answer is Monday

qs.situation: A manager asks for the date 3 working days BEFORE a Wednesday deadline, to know when work must start.
options: Count back normally, giving the previous Friday
Counting backwards is not allowed; no date is given
Count back but never land earlier than today

qs.situation: A customer was born on 29 February 2000. On 28 February 2024 (not yet a birthday), how old do you say they are?
options: 23, since the birthday has not come yet; they turn 24 on 1 March in years with no 29 February
23 until 29 February arrives; in years with no 29 February they turn older on 28 February
Treated as a birthday on 28 February, so 24

qs.situation: Someone's birth date is entered as next year by mistake, so they appear not yet born.
options: Show nothing (blank) so someone checks the entry
Show an age of 0
Show a clear warning instead of an age

qs.situation: A wellness report shows a staff member's body mass index as 24.96.
options: Show 25.0, rounded to one decimal place
Show 25, a whole number
Show 24.96, two decimal places

qs.situation: A wrong entry gives a height of 5 cm for a 70 kg person, producing a body mass index of 2800.
options: Show the silly number as is; the data entry is the problem
Show nothing (blank) when the numbers are not believable (for example height under 100 cm or over 250 cm)
Show a clear warning that the entry looks wrong

qs.situation: A client's invoice of 1,000 dollars is 10 days late. What penalty do you charge?
options: A one-time 5% fee, so 50 dollars, however many days late
1.5% for every 30 days late, spread out day by day, never more than the invoice itself
A flat 25 dollars no matter the amount or the days

qs.situation: An invoice is only 2 days late and the client is a long-standing friend of the business.
options: Charge the full penalty from day 1; no grace period
Allow a grace of 5 days, no penalty until after that
Allow a grace of 15 days, no penalty until after that

qs.situation: A customer has a credit of 200 dollars on their account (they are owed money) and the invoice shows as late.
options: No penalty: 0.00
Penalty is worked out on the invoice anyway
Nothing is shown (blank) so someone looks at the account

qs.situation: A student scores 89.6 out of 100 and the cut-off for an A is 90.
options: B: the exact score is used and not rounded up
A: the score is rounded to the nearest whole mark first
A: anything within one mark of the cut-off is lifted up

qs.situation: A student scores 85 out of 100. Does your school use plus and minus grades?
options: No: A 90+, B 80+, C 70+, D 60+, F below 60, so 85 is a B
Yes: for example 87+ is B+, 83 to 86 is B, below 83 is B-
Different cut-offs: A 85+, B 70+, C 55+, D 40+, F below 40

qs.situation: A student scores 105 out of 100 because of extra credit.
options: A: anything above full marks is an A
A, but the score is first capped at 100
Nothing is shown (blank) because the score looks like an error

qs.situation: A receipt shows a customer's card number. How much of it can be seen?
options: Only the last 4 digits
The first 6 and last 4 digits
Only the last 2 digits

qs.situation: A card number is entered with only 3 digits, for example a mistyped code.
options: Mask all of it, never show anything
Show it exactly as typed, since it is too short to be a real card
Show nothing at all (blank)

qs.situation: A 50 dollar item has a promotion of 120% off because someone mistyped the discount.
options: Price is 0.00; any discount above 100% counts as 100%
Nothing is shown (blank) so someone fixes the promotion
Price is the full 50 dollars; the odd discount is ignored

qs.situation: The price on a product is negative, for example -20 dollars, because of a refund or data error.
options: Nothing is shown (blank); a negative price is invalid
Show the negative price after discount as given
Treat it as 0.00

qs.situation: Shipping a parcel to zone B. What is the charge structure?
options: 5.00 base plus 1.00 per kg for A, 2.00 for B, 3.00 for C
A flat price per zone, whatever the weight
Different base charges per zone, which we will give you

qs.situation: A parcel weighs 1.2 kg.
options: Charged as 2 kg: always rounded up to the next whole kilo
Charged as 1 kg: part kilos are dropped
Charged by the exact weight, 1.2 kg

qs.situation: A customer wants to ship a 80 kg crate, heavier than any parcel you normally take.
options: Price it by the same formula, no weight limit
Refuse; nothing is shown above 30 kg
Refuse above 30 kg and ask for a special quote

qs.situation: A product page is titled "Bob's Fish & Chips -- 50% Off!"
options: bobs-fish-chips-50-off: apostrophes removed, & and symbols become hyphens
bob-s-fish-and-chips-50-off: apostrophes become hyphens and & becomes 'and'
bobs-fish-and-chips-50-percent-off: & and % are spelled out as words

qs.situation: A product is called "Café 日本 Tea" and the Japanese characters have no plain-English letters.
options: cafe-tea: accents become plain letters and the Japanese is dropped
cafe-ri-ben-tea: Japanese is spelled out in English letters
The whole title is left alone and the web address keeps the original characters

qs.situation: Two different products, "Blue Shirt" and "Blue-Shirt!", end up with the same web address.
options: Both get the same address; the team makes them unique by hand
The second one gets a number added, like blue-shirt-2
Refuse the second; someone must retitle it

qs.situation: A product has ratings of 5, 4 and 4, an average of 4.33. What is the headline rating?
options: 4.3: rounded to one decimal place, half up
4.5: rounded to the nearest half star
4: rounded to a whole star

qs.situation: A product gets a rating of 0 and another of 7, both outside the 1 to 5 range.
options: Ignore them and use only ratings from 1 to 5
Count a 0 as 1 and a 7 as 5
Show nothing (blank) for the product until someone checks the data

qs.situation: A new product has no ratings yet, or only blank ones.
options: Show nothing (blank), not zero stars
Show 0 stars
Show a default of 3 stars until real ratings arrive

qs.situation: A brand new product has just one review, a single 5-star rating.
options: Show 5.0 as it is
Show nothing until there are at least 3 ratings
Pull it toward the store average until more ratings come in
